remit: X12 defines this reason as an expired time limit for filing. For Original Medicare fee-for-service, 42 CFR 424.44 sets the limit at the end of one calendar year after the date of service. Other payers set their own limits.

extraSources.label: 42 CFR 424.44, time limits for filing claims

metaDescription: CO-29 denial explained: the time limit for filing has expired. What proof helps an appeal, how filing limits differ by payer, and how to prevent it.
summary: The payer says the claim reached it after the filing deadline.
causes: An earlier submission was rejected and never fixed
The practice did not track filing limits for each payer
fixes: Gather proof of timely filing, such as a clearinghouse acceptance report or earlier payer response
Appeal with that proof, following the payer's appeal process
If no proof exists, ask your billing lead whether any adjustment is allowed under your contract
prevention: Track filing limits by payer; Medicare generally allows 12 months from the date of service, and other payers vary
Work rejections the same day so claims are not lost

faqs.question: What is the Medicare timely filing limit?
faqs.answer: Medicare generally requires claims within 12 months of the date of service. Commercial payers set their own limits, often shorter.

faqs.question: Can a CO-29 denial be overturned?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, with proof the claim was filed on time or that a payer error caused the delay. Without proof, it is hard to win.
